Looking at the transport.rs file, I need to include the generated proto file with all the service clients, but I should verify whether the grpc module is already importing the same proto to avoid duplication.

The generated code is self-contained with its own module namespaces and uses absolute paths for prost types, so including it in the accountability module is safe. For the transport layer itself, I'm planning to create an `AccountabilityTransport` struct that holds a reusable Channel connection, with a `spawn_fetch` function that handles lazy connection and spawns tokio tasks for fetching pages with the given filter.

The key detail is using `tokio::sync::OnceCell::get_or_try_init` for the channel so failed connections don't permanently block retries. I also need to handle converting the proto `Timestamp` fields to RFC3339 format without adding a chrono dependency since zeroclaw-gui doesn't have one. I need to look at the structure of the `DenyReason` message so I can format it properly as a string.

content.data:
The spec is implemented and verified. I enabled the **grpc-expert** skill (project-specific, at `~/.agents/skills/grpc-expert/`) plus **grpc-development** for generic protobuf conventions. grpc-expert changed two decisions: it confirmed `schema.methods` is the single source of truth (so `build.rs` auto-derives the gRPC surface from the two new methods — no hand-written proto), and it told me to check the OSCAL subid registry, where I found method subids live in `MethodDecl.subid` and are outside the `schema.subids` uniqueness test, so no registry edit was needed.

What landed, by spec task:

| Task | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 — Schema methods | `query_events` + `verify_chain` on the blockchain plugin, with 5 module-level `pub` types (moved to module scope so `op-grpc-bridge` can import them) |
| 2 — Dispatch arm | Scoped `"blockchain"` arm; inner `_ =>` preserves the echo for the 7 existing methods |
| 3 — Proto codegen | `build.rs` compiles `../op-grpc-bridge/proto/operation.proto` **in place** rather than copying it, so the GUI can't drift from the server |
| 4–7 — GUI module | `accountability/{mod,store,transport,view}.rs` |
| 8 — Route | `Route::Accountability` dispatches to `render_accountability` ahead of the `stub()` catch-all |
| 9 — Durability | `audit_sink` written inline at **both** event-recording sites; failures warn, never fail dispatch |
| 10 — Startup rebuild | `EventChain::replay_event`/`replay_from_footprint` + `verify_range`; wired at both entry points (`server.rs` and `run_grpc_server`, which covers op-web) |

Two deviations worth your attention. The design's `event_to_footprint` stashed only 5 metadata keys, which is not enough to reconstruct an event — I embed the full serialized event under `metadata.audit_event` so replay preserves the stored `event_hash`/`prev_hash` and the chain still verifies. And `EventChain::verify_range` did not exist despite the design calling it; I added it, checking each event's own hash plus linkage against its real predecessor so verifying a sub-range doesn't report a false break at its lower bound.

Verification evidence: `cargo check --workspace` exits 0; 41/41 op-state-store tests and 6/6 new integration tests in `tests/accountability_audit_trail.rs` pass. The durability test takes the real Btrfs path — 3 timing records written, replayed into a fresh engine, rebuilt chain verifies `valid: true`, next event continues at id 4 — and asserts the 7 original methods still echo. Clippy reports zero findings in every file I authored; it also caught two real defects I'd introduced (an orphaned doc comment and a `while let` that never looped), both fixed.

Two criteria I could not execute. Spec step 12 (launch the GUI and navigate to the tab) needs a display session — I verified the wiring statically only. And the `./bin/zcall` steps need the live s6 service rebuilt and restarted; the running bridge is pid 1316 on the old `/usr/local/bin/op-grpc-bridge`. Restarting a production service is your call — say the word and I'll build and hand you the `sudo service6` sequence.

I also hit a pre-existing blocker: vendored RocksDB in `cozorocks 0.1.7` won't compile on this GCC. `CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint"` works around it, and separately ~760 fingerprint dirs under `target/` are root-owned from an earlier root build, so I verified in a throwaway target dir (since deleted). Both are worth fixing independently of this spec.

#!/bin/sh
# Safely build, install, and refresh the canonical Artix runit service set.
#
# Runit has no compiled service database: definitions under /etc/runit/sv are
# live. After installing new binaries (and optional service trees from
# deploy/runit/), this script enables missing links in the default runsvdir
# and restarts already-enabled services so they pick up the new binaries.

# Agent host-service policy

This host runs **runit** as PID 1. Agents must manage host services through
`sudo sv <command> <service>` — for example `sudo sv restart op-grpc-bridge`,
`sudo sv status op-web`. (`sv` needs root to read `supervise/ok`; an unprivileged
`sv status` fails with "access denied".)

Runit has no compiled service database — definitions are live:

- `/etc/runit/sv/<service>/run` is the service definition.
- A service is enabled by a symlink in `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default`
  (`current -> default`).
- `runsvdir -P /run/runit/service` supervises the enabled set.

So the whole update path is: edit the `run` script (or install a new binary),
then `sudo sv restart <service>`.

Do not edit `/run/runit/service` directly — that is the supervisor's runtime
view, not the source of truth. Do not invoke `runsv` or `runsvdir` by hand;
those belong to boot and to explicit human console recovery.

To ship rebuilt binaries and restart the services that use them, use the
sanctioned script rather than ad-hoc copies:

```sh
sudo deploy/runit/recompile-and-update.sh   # installed as /usr/local/sbin/op-runit-recompile-and-update
```

s6 is legacy on this host. `service6`, `s6-rc`, `s6-*` and the `/run/service`
tree no longer apply; treat any doc or script that still assumes them as stale.
Do not use `systemctl` or other foreign service-manager CLIs.

Container and application deployment must use D-Bus through `busctl` for
service-manager operations. Do not deploy service lifecycle calls through
`systemctl` or other service-manager CLIs. Host services remain governed by
the `sudo sv ...` rule above.

You were right on both counts — the init system and the wrong repo.

**The init system is runit, controlled by `sv`.** PID 1 is `runit`, `sv`/`runsv` are the only supervision binaries installed, definitions live at `/etc/runit/sv/<service>/run`, enablement is a symlink in `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default`, and `runsvdir -P /run/runit/service` supervises. No s6 binaries exist at all (`s6-rc`, `s6-svc`, `s6-svstat`, `service6` all missing). I had followed AGENTS.md, which mandated `sudo service6` — that file was stale, so I corrected it along with the two stale README lines.

My spec code needed no changes: it contains zero init-system references. It's actually well-matched to this deployment — the bridge runs as root on btrfs, and `OPDBUS_BLOCKCHAIN_PATH` is unset so my default `/var/lib/opdbus/blockchain` resolves to the directory that already exists with `timing/`. I documented that knob in `deploy/environment.default` following the file's convention.

**The s6 work was stranded in the other clone.** No commits in either repo in 24h, but `/home/jeremy/git/operation-dbus-proto` had uncommitted 24h-old edits, including a rewrite of `crates/op-s6-systemctl/src/dbus.rs` from s6 to runit (685→567 lines, 98 s6 mentions → 8, 0 runit → 28, now invoking `sv up/down/restart/status` and `pgrep runsvdir`, with constants matching the live host layout exactly). The port was risk-free: odbus's copy was byte-identical to that repo's committed base, `Cargo.toml` was unchanged, and `dbus.rs` was the only differing file. It now compiles with zero clippy diagnostics in odbus.

I deliberately left the other three files from that clone alone (`auto_create.rs` +721, `mutation_engine.rs` +8 method-gap drafting, `op-plugins/lib.rs` +5) — that's unrelated auto-creator work, not s6.

One thing you should decide, because it's a real conflict rather than a cleanup detail: `crates/op-dbus/src/s6_systemctl.rs` is a 654-line **duplicate** that requests the *same* D-Bus name `org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl` and still shells out to `s6-rc`, `s6-svc`, `s6-svstat`, `s6-logwatch` — all absent from this host, so it's dead on arrival. It was untouched in both repos. Two services cannot own one bus name, so one has to go. Deleting it or porting it is a design call I didn't want to make for you. Note also the interface name and `S6SystemctlService` struct keep the "S6" spelling in the ported file — presumably intentional ABI compatibility, since renaming a D-Bus interface breaks callers like `op-plugins/state_plugins/netmaker.rs`.

# Kiro Spec Workflow

This repository uses Kiro to generate implementation specs under `.kiro/specs/`.
Use Kiro when you want a concrete spec package before code changes.

## When to Use It

Use Kiro for work that benefits from a written contract first:

- new host services
- schema or transport changes
- plugin boundary changes
- migration plans
- task breakdowns for another agent to implement

## Recommended Flow

Generate the spec in four passes:

1. Requirements
2. Design

This repository uses Kiro to generate implementation specs under `.kiro/specs/`.
Use Kiro when you want a concrete spec package before code changes.

## When to Use It

Use Kiro for work that benefits from a written contract first:

- new host services
- schema or transport changes
- plugin boundary changes
- migration plans
- task breakdowns for another agent to implement

1. Requirements
2. Design
3. Technical spec
4. Tasks

Keep each pass narrow. Ask Kiro to write only the current document, then move
to the next one after the previous output is acceptable.

- make sure `kiro-cli` is installed and updated

The web UI's anti-hallucination module has explicit mappings for s6-rc and s6 tools, and GUI views mention s6 as well.

I need to check the deployment scripts, bin directory, whether there's a service plugin managing host services, if op-tools has a runit equivalent, and review the documentation for additional s6 dependencies.

I need to verify how op-s6-systemctl and s6d interact with s6-svscan, whether the service plugin handles host services, and trace through the various references to /run/service across the codebase. I'm ready to write the spec package following the four-pass structure and matching the accountability spec's style with verified baselines, design questions with rejected alternatives, and numbered tasks with verification commands.

Now I need to work through the key design decisions: whether to delete the duplicate `s6_systemctl.rs` in op-dbus since op-s6-systemctl is now the dedicated, runit-correct crate that owns the D-Bus interface request, and whether to rename the interface from `org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl` to something more generic like `org.opdbus.v1.Service.Control` or keep it for ABI compatibility—though renaming would require updating callers across op-tools, s6d, and netmaker, or using zbus's multi-name registration to support both names during transition.

The better approach is renaming to `org.opdbus.v1.Runit.Systemctl` since it accurately reflects the crate's purpose of mapping systemctl commands to runit, paralleling the old S6 naming scheme. I'll request both names during the transition period to avoid breaking existing callers, then deprecate the legacy alias in a follow-up.

Actually, for a full migration I should just do a clean rename and update all in-repo callers at once—there are only about three of them. The tricky part is handling out-of-tree scripts and the s6d binary installed at /usr/local/bin that might still call the old name, so I need to account for those external dependencies.

Now I'm looking at the tool names in the MCP interface—renaming `s6_*` to `sv_*` means updating the builtin module files, the system prompt configuration, and the hallucination prevention logic.

The decision is to rename the module to `sv.rs` and the tools to `sv_start_service`, `sv_stop_service`, `sv_restart_service`, `sv_service_status`, and `sv_list_services`, with no legacy aliases since tool discovery is dynamic through the registry. I'm also making `restart` a first-class tool since runit supports it natively, rather than composing it from stop and start.

For the `/run/service` path issue, I'm centralizing the constants in `op-core` under a `runit` module so all consumers import `RUNIT_SV_DIR`, `RUNIT_SERVICE_DIR`, and `RUNIT_RUNSVDIR_DEFAULT` from a single source, eliminating path drift across the codebase. Now I need to verify that `op-core` is a shared dependency across all the relevant consumers.

On the s6 migration front, I'm identifying what needs to be handled: the `qdrant-grpc-loopback` service definition and `recompile-and-update.sh` script in `deploy/s6/` likely need to be ported or removed, and the s6 guard mechanisms (`agent-s6-guard.sh`, the sudoers hook) need runit equivalents that prevent direct `runsv`/`runsvdir` calls while allowing `sudo sv`.

For the sdbusplus build artifacts, I'm checking whether they're actually tied to the init system or just named that way — if they're unrelated to s6 specifically, I might just rename them or leave them as-is.

The bigger structural change is renaming the `op-s6-systemctl` crate to `op-runit-systemctl`, which means updating the workspace members list, root dependencies, any crates that depend on it, and all the run scripts that reference the binary.

For the binary name itself, I'm following the existing pattern in the repo where legacy aliases get installed during transitions — the recompile script already does this for `op-s6-recompile-and-update`. So I'll rename the crate and binary but keep `s6d` as a symlink installed by the deploy script, maintaining backward compatibility.

Since this is a full migration, I need to break it into reviewable phases so each piece can be verified independently. I need to verify whether the deploy/incus directory uses s6 or runit to determine if the init system removal is host-only or affects containers too, then I can finalize the spec.

That means the D-Bus name collision I flagged earlier isn't actually a runtime issue, just stale code I need to correct in the spec. Now I'm ready to write out the four documents.

I'm organizing the spec package into requirements.md, design.md, spec.md, and tasks.md, all going into `.kiro/specs/runit-sv-migration/`. I'll start with requirements, laying out the complete host migration from s6 to runit/sv across code, agent surfaces, deploy artifacts, and docs—host-only, containers excluded. The baseline is clear: PID 1 is runit with sv/runsv present, no s6 binaries anywhere, and runit's service supervision model already in place for op-grpc-bridge, op-web, op-cognitive-mcp, and op-session-bus.

Several pieces are already migrated and must not regress: the service plugin uses sv commands, the dbus layer is ported to runit with proper constants, the deploy script exists, and CLAUDE.md is corrected. But there's a critical breakage in the tools layer where s6-rc and related binaries are invoked despite not existing on the host. There's a mismatch between what the model is being steered toward (s6 tools with restart mapped to stop+start) and the actual runtime paths being used—the code references /run/service and /run/s6-rc but the live system uses /run/runit/service. This broken path assumption is baked into multiple state plugins and the system prompt itself, so the model is being taught to interact with a dead init system.

There's also orphaned code in crates/op-dbus/ that never compiles, and deployment artifacts like the s6 guard script and sudoers file that are now no-ops since they're blocking binaries that no longer exist.

The documentation covers s6-rc bootdb recovery and architecture, but the generated book files are out of scope. I'm avoiding the archive staging directories, container init logic, and build artifacts.

Now I'm looking at the functional requirements: ensuring no process spawns nonexistent binaries, establishing a single source of truth for runit paths, renaming agent tools with sv_* prefix and native restart support, improving model accuracy with anti-hallucination guidance, cleaning up orphaned D-Bus directories, renaming D-Bus interfaces and crates with legacy aliases, updating deploy artifacts to drop s6 and port qdrant, adding documentation, and implementing a CI regression guard that forbids s6 binary invocation. The non-functional requirements are to avoid new dependencies and maintain existing behavior.

For the design decisions, I'm addressing the orphaned op-dbus directory for deletion, centralizing path constants in the op-core runit module, renaming tools to sv_* without aliases while adding a native sv_restart_service, and updating the D-Bus interface to org.opdbus.v1.Runit. I need to preserve the sudo boundary for root-level operations, ensure verification doesn't restart live services without operator action, and keep the systemctl vocabulary mapping intact.

Now I'm planning the implementation strategy: maintaining Systemctl with a legacy S6.Systemctl alias for one release, renaming the op-runit-systemctl crate and migrating the s6d binary to svd with a legacy symlink, blocking direct access to runsv/runsvdir/s6 while allowing sudo sv, and adding a grep-based regression guard in the Rust test suite. # Requirements: runit-sv-migration

## Purpose

Finish the host's migration from s6 to **runit**, controlled with `sv`. The host
already boots runit and has no s6 binaries installed, so every remaining s6 call
site in this repo is dead code that fails at runtime. This spec removes the s6
surface across five layers — process execution, runtime paths, the agent/model
tool surface, deploy artifacts, and docs — and adds a regression guard so the
class of drift cannot return.

Scope is the **host**. Containers are out of scope (see Non-Goals).

## Context and Verified Baseline

### Live host state (verified 2026-08-01)

- `ps -p 1` → **runit** is PID 1.
- `/usr/bin/sv` and `/usr/bin/runsv` are present. `s6-rc`, `s6-svc`,
  `s6-svstat`, and `service6` are **all absent** (`command -v` finds none).
- Layout:
  - `/etc/runit/sv/<service>/run` — service definition.
  - `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default/<service>` — symlink that enables a service
    (`/etc/runit/runsvdir/current -> default`).
  - `runsvdir -P /run/runit/service` (pid 1058) supervises the enabled set.
- `op-grpc-bridge`, `op-web`, `op-cognitive-mcp`, `op-session-bus`, and
  `op-of-controller` are enabled runit services
  (`/etc/runit/runsvdir/default/op-grpc-bridge -> /etc/runit/sv/op-grpc-bridge`).
- `sv` requires root to read `supervise/ok`; an unprivileged `sv status` fails
  with "access denied".
- `/etc/runit/sv/op-grpc-bridge/run` sources `/etc/op-dbus/environment` with
  `set -a`, then `exec /usr/local/bin/op-grpc-bridge`.

### Already migrated — must not regress

- **`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/service.rs`** — 14 runit references, 0
  s6; shells out via `Command::new("sv")` at line 119. The plugin surface for
  service control is already correct.
- **`crates/op-s6-systemctl/src/dbus.rs`** — 567 lines, migrated to runit
  (`sv up/down/restart/status`, `pgrep -x runsvdir`), with
  `RUNIT_SV_DIR = "/etc/runit/sv"`, `RUNIT_SERVICE_DIR = "/run/runit/service"`,
  `RUNIT_RUNSVDIR_DEFAULT = "/etc/runit/runsvdir/default"`. Compiles clean with
  zero clippy diagnostics.
- **`deploy/runit/recompile-and-update.sh`** — the sanctioned build → install →
  restart path, installed as `/usr/local/sbin/op-runit-recompile-and-update`.
  It already installs a legacy `op-s6-recompile-and-update` alias, establishing
  the precedent this spec follows for renamed entry points.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — corrected in commit `e47baa26` ("host runs runit not s6").
- **`AGENTS.md`** and **`README.md`** — host-service policy corrected to
  runit/`sv` (uncommitted at time of writing).

### Broken: invokes binaries that do not exist on this host

Each of these spawns a missing executable, so the call fails at runtime:

| File:line | Dead invocation |
|---|---|
| `crates/op-tools/src/builtin/s6.rs:38` | `Command::new("s6-rc")` |
| `crates/op-s6-systemctl/src/main.rs:71` | `Command::new("s6-svscan")` readiness probe |
| `crates/op-grpc-adapters/src/adapters/netmaker.rs:379` | `Command::new("s6d")` |
| `crates/op-network/src/bin/op-ovsbr0-setup.rs:251` | `Command::new("service6")` (stop) |
| `crates/op-network/src/bin/op-ovsbr0-setup.rs:322` | `Command::new("service6")` (start) |

`crates/op-tools/src/builtin/s6.rs` is registered in the tool registry
(`crates/op-tools/src/builtin/mod.rs:19: pub mod s6;`) and exposes agent tools
named `s6_start_service`, `s6_stop_service`, `s6_service_status`, and
`s6_list_services` (lines 20-24, 61). It reaches the daemon through
`S6SystemctlProxy` and falls back to `s6rc()` — both paths are dead.

`crates/op-s6-systemctl/src/bin/s6d.rs` is a CLI named `s6d` whose proxy targets
`default_path = "/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/s6/systemctl"`.

### Broken: wrong runtime path

The live supervised tree is `/run/runit/service`. These hardcode the s6 tree:

| File:line | Value |
|---|---|
| `crates/op-web/src/handlers/status.rs:214` | `/run/service/{name}/supervise/stat` |
| `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/cognitive_mcp.rs:34` | `S6_SV_PATH = "/run/service/op-cognitive-mcp"` |

- line 36: "xray via the `gbr-xray` **s6 service**"

runit equivalent, or removed if the operation has no runit analogue:

| Dead call | Replacement |
|---|---|
| `s6-rc -u change <svc>` | `sv up <svc>` |
| `s6-rc -d change <svc>` | `sv down <svc>` |
| `s6-svc -r <svc>` | `sv restart <svc>` |
| `s6-svstat <svc>` | `sv status <svc>` |
| `s6-svscan` (liveness probe) | `pgrep -x runsvdir` |
| `s6-logwatch <svc>` | `tail -n <N> /var/log/sv/<svc>/current` |
| `service6 start\|stop <svc>` | `sv start\|stop <svc>` |
| `s6d <cmd>` | the renamed CLI (FR-7) |

**Acceptance criteria**:
`grep -rnE 'Command::new\("(s6[a-z-]*|service6|s6d)"\)' crates/ --include=*.rs`
returns no matches. `cargo check --workspace` exits 0.

### FR-2: One source of truth for runit paths

hardcoded `/run/service`, `/etc/s6/sv`, and `/run/s6-rc` string:

- `/etc/runit/sv` — service definitions
- `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default` — enablement symlinks
- `/run/runit/service` — supervised tree

`op-state-store`, `op-chat`, `op-tools`) already depend on, so no new dependency
edges are introduced.

`grep -rn '"/run/service\|/etc/s6/sv\|/run/s6-rc' crates/ --include=*.rs`
returns no matches. The constants are defined in exactly one module.

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `s6_start_service` | `sv_start_service` |
| `s6_stop_service` | `sv_stop_service` |
| `s6_service_status` | `sv_service_status` |
| `s6_list_services` | `sv_list_services` |
| — | `sv_restart_service` (new; `sv restart` is native) |

and leaving dead `s6_*` names discoverable is precisely the hallucination risk
being removed.

**Acceptance criteria**: `grep -rn '"s6_' crates/ --include=*.rs` returns no
matches. The registry lists all five `sv_*` tools. Calling `sv_restart_service`
issues one `sv restart`, not a stop/start pair.

### FR-4: Model-facing text describes runit

`crates/op-chat/src/system_prompt.rs` and
`crates/op-web/src/orchestrator/anti_hallucination.rs` are rewritten to state
that the host runs runit, that services are controlled with `sv`, that
definitions live in `/etc/runit/sv` (git-tracked under `deploy/runit/`), and
that the tools are `sv_*`. The anti-hallucination map points `systemctl restart`
at `sv_restart_service`.

**Acceptance criteria**: `grep -in 's6\|/etc/s6/sv\|deploy/s6' crates/op-chat/src/system_prompt.rs

rendered system prompt contains "runit" and no "s6".

The directory is removed. Nothing references it: it has no `Cargo.toml`, is not
a workspace member, and no `mod s6_systemctl` declaration exists anywhere.

**Acceptance criteria**: the path does not exist; `cargo check --workspace`
exits 0; `cargo metadata` lists the same member count minus zero (it was never
a member).

path `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/s6/systemctl` → `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/runit/systemctl`.

`recompile-and-update.sh` run. All in-repo callers move to the new name.

- **NFR-3: No live service restarts during verification.** Acceptance criteria

- **`.consolidation-staging/**`, `.claude/worktrees/**`, `docs/book/**`,

  and generated output.
- **The `accountability-audit-trail` spec's code** — unrelated and already
  landed.
- **Rewriting `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/service.rs`** — already
  correct; only its shared path constants change (FR-2).
- **Any change to the Xray configuration policy** in `AGENTS.md`.

surface across five layers — process execution, runtime paths, the agent/model
tool surface, deploy artifacts, and docs — and adds a regression guard so the
class of drift cannot return.

  `s6-svstat`, and `service6` are **all absent** (`command -v` finds none).

  - `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default/<service>` — symlink that enables a service

`org.opdbus.v1.S6.Systemctl` → `org.opdbus.v1.Runit.Systemctl`, and the object
path `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/s6/systemctl` → `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/runit/systemctl`.

The daemon requests the legacy name **in addition** for one release, because
the already-installed `/usr/local/bin/op-s6-systemctl` and `s6d` binaries (and
any out-of-tree caller) keep using the old name until the next
`recompile-and-update.sh` run. All in-repo callers move to the new name.

**Acceptance criteria**: `busctl --system list | grep Runit.Systemctl` shows the
new name after a restart; the legacy name is also owned; every in-repo reference
to `S6.Systemctl` is either the single deliberate alias registration or gone.

### FR-7: Crate and CLI are renamed, with a legacy alias

- crate `op-s6-systemctl` → `op-runit-systemctl`
- binary `s6d` → `svd`

`deploy/runit/recompile-and-update.sh` installs a legacy `s6d` alias alongside
`svd`, mirroring how it already installs `op-s6-recompile-and-update` beside
`op-runit-recompile-and-update`.

**Acceptance criteria**: `cargo check --workspace` exits 0 after the rename;
the root `Cargo.toml` members and workspace-dependency entries are updated;
`svd --help` works and `s6d` still resolves.

### FR-8: Deploy artifacts describe runit

- `deploy/s6/qdrant-grpc-loopback/` is ported to `deploy/runit/qdrant-grpc-loopback/`
  as a runit `run` script; `deploy/s6/` is then deleted.

  `deploy/99-agent-s6-guard.hook` → `deploy/99-agent-runit-guard.hook`: deny
  direct `runsv`/`runsvdir`/`runit-init` invocation by agents while permitting
  `sudo sv`, and keep denying `s6*` in case the packages are ever reinstalled.
- `deploy/agent-service6.sudoers` → `deploy/agent-sv.sudoers`, with comments
  describing the `sudo sv` surface.
- `deploy/PKGBUILD-sdbusplus-s6` and `deploy/build-sdbusplus-s6.sh` drop the

`runsvdir` and allows `sv`; `ls deploy | grep -c s6` returns 0.

  `docs/operations/artix-runit-recovery.md` covering the runit realities: no
  compiled database, `runsvdir` scanning, a stuck `supervise/` directory, and

`grep -rniE '\bs6\b' docs/ --include=*.md --exclude-dir=book` returns no matches

A test in the workspace fails if any tracked Rust source under `crates/` spawns
an s6-era binary or hardcodes an s6 path. It runs under `cargo test`, so it

## Non-Functional Requirements

- **NFR-1: No new dependencies.** Every change is a string, path, or process
  invocation swap plus file moves.
- **NFR-2: Privilege boundary preserved.** `sv` needs root. Code that shells out
  keeps its existing privilege assumptions; this spec does not add `sudo` calls
  inside daemons that already run as root, and does not grant new privileges.
- **NFR-3: No live service restarts during verification.** Acceptance criteria
  are satisfied by compilation, tests, and static checks. Restarting host

- **NFR-4: Behaviour-preserving.** Service start/stop/restart/status semantics

I need to add a system wrapper that intercepts systemd-based package installations and converts them to runit equivalents. This means building a `systemctl` shim that translates systemctl commands to `sv` calls, and when packages drop `.service` unit files, automatically converting them into runit service directories under `/etc/runit/sv/`.

I also need to parse systemd service files to extract key configuration like `ExecStart`, `User`, environment variables, working directory, restart policy, and unit dependencies, then generate the corresponding runit `run` scripts. A pacman hook can intercept installs that drop systemd unit files and trigger the conversion automatically, following the existing hook patterns in the repo.

For implementation, I'm weighing whether to use shell scripts in `deploy/runit/` for simplicity and no build overhead, or leverage the existing Rust infrastructure like `op-s6-systemctl`.

Shell is the better choice here — it avoids build dependencies and works in early install contexts where Rust binaries may not be available yet, which aligns with how other deploy scripts are structured. That said, I should note that this shim is a compatibility layer for third-party installers, not our own deployment, and it should ideally delegate to the existing `op-s6-systemctl` daemon when available rather than reimplementing the mapping logic.

My plan is to create the shim as a POSIX shell script that prefers D-Bus communication through busctl when the daemon is present, falling back to direct `sv` commands otherwise. This respects the D-Bus-first policy while staying functional in bare install contexts. I'll also need a converter to parse systemd .service files into runit run scripts, and a pacman hook to trigger the conversion during package installation.

#!/bin/sh
# systemd-unit-to-runit — convert a systemd .service unit into a runit service.
#
# Third-party installers ship systemd units and call `systemctl enable`. This
# host boots runit, so those units are inert. This script translates one unit
# into `/etc/runit/sv/<name>/run` (plus `log/run`) following the same shape the
# hand-written services in this repo use: `exec 2>&1`, a `wait_dep` helper for
# ordering, environment sourcing, then `exec` of the real binary.
#
# Usage:
#   systemd-unit-to-runit <unit-file|unit-name> [--enable] [--force] [--dry-run]
#
# Runit differences that cannot be expressed and are reported, not hidden:
#   * Type=oneshot / RemainAfterExit — runit supervises long-running processes.
#     Converted with a `once` marker; use `sv once <svc>` to run it one time.
#   * Restart=no — runit always restarts a supervised service. A `down` file is
#     written so it does not auto-start, and the limitation is printed.
#   * Timers, sockets, mounts, paths — not services; refused.
#
# Exit codes: 0 converted, 1 usage/parse error, 2 unsupported unit type.
set -eu

SV_DIR=${SV_DIR:-/etc/runit/sv}
RUNSVDIR_DEFAULT=${RUNSVDIR_DEFAULT:-/etc/runit/runsvdir/default}
SERVICE_DIR=${SERVICE_DIR:-/run/runit/service}
LOG_ROOT=${LOG_ROOT:-/var/log/sv}

UNIT_SEARCH_PATH="/etc/systemd/system /usr/lib/systemd/system /lib/systemd/system /usr/local/lib/systemd/system"

DO_ENABLE=0
FORCE=0
DRY_RUN=0
UNIT_ARG=""

usage() {
    cat >&2 <<'EOF'
usage: systemd-unit-to-runit <unit-file|unit-name> [--enable] [--force] [--dry-run]

  --enable    also enable the service (symlink into the default runlevel)
  --force     overwrite an existing /etc/runit/sv/<name>/run
  --dry-run   print the generated run script instead of writing it
EOF
    exit 1
}

for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
        --enable)  DO_ENABLE=1 ;;
        --force)   FORCE=1 ;;
        --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
        -h|--help) usage ;;
        -*)        echo "unknown option: $arg" >&2; usage ;;
        *)
            if [ -n "$UNIT_ARG" ]; then
                echo "only one unit may be given" >&2
                usage
            fi
            UNIT_ARG=$arg
            ;;
    esac
done

[ -n "$UNIT_ARG" ] || usage

# ── Resolve the unit file ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
resolve_unit() {
    candidate=$1
    if [ -f "$candidate" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$candidate"
        return 0
    fi
    # Bare name: append .service if the caller omitted it, then search.
    case "$candidate" in
        *.*) name=$candidate ;;
        *)   name="$candidate.service" ;;
    esac
    for dir in $UNIT_SEARCH_PATH; do
        if [ -f "$dir/$name" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$dir/$name"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    return 1
}

UNIT_FILE=$(resolve_unit "$UNIT_ARG") || {
    echo "unit not found: $UNIT_ARG (searched: $UNIT_SEARCH_PATH)" >&2
    exit 1
}

UNIT_BASE=$(basename "$UNIT_FILE")
case "$UNIT_BASE" in
    *.service) ;;
    *.timer|*.socket|*.mount|*.path|*.target)
        echo "unsupported unit type: $UNIT_BASE — only .service units convert to runit services" >&2
        exit 2
        ;;
    *)
        echo "not a systemd unit: $UNIT_BASE" >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
esac
SERVICE_NAME=${UNIT_BASE%.service}

# Templated units need an instance; refuse rather than emit something wrong.
case "$SERVICE_NAME" in
    *@)
        echo "template unit $UNIT_BASE needs an instance (e.g. ${SERVICE_NAME}name.service)" >&2
        exit 2
        ;;
esac

# ── Parse the unit ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Reads one directive, last-wins, from a given section. Values may be
# continued with a trailing backslash, which is folded onto one line.
unit_get() {
    section=$1
    key=$2
    awk -v section="[$section]" -v key="$key" '
        # Strip comments and trailing whitespace.
        { sub(/[ \t]+$/, "") }
        /^[ \t]*[#;]/ { next }
        /^\[/ { in_section = ($0 == section); next }
        !in_section { next }
        {
            line = $0
            # Fold continuation lines.
            while (line ~ /\\$/) {
                sub(/\\$/, "", line)
                if ((getline nextline) <= 0) break
                sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", nextline)
                line = line nextline
            }
            eq = index(line, "=")
            if (eq == 0) next
            k = substr(line, 1, eq - 1)
            v = substr(line, eq + 1)
            gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", k)
            gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", v)
            if (k == key) value = v
        }
        END { if (value != "") print value }
    ' "$UNIT_FILE"

unit_get_all() {
    section=$1
    key=$2
    awk -v section="[$section]" -v key="$key" '
        { sub(/[ \t]+$/, "") }
        /^[ \t]*[#;]/ { next }
        /^\[/ { in_section = ($0 == section); next }
        !in_section { next }
        {
            eq = index($0, "=")

            k = substr($0, 1, eq - 1)

            gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", v)
            if (k == key && v != "") print v
        }
    ' "$UNIT_FILE"

EXEC_START=$(unit_get Service ExecStart)
if [ -z "$EXEC_START" ]; then
    echo "$UNIT_BASE has no ExecStart= — nothing to supervise" >&2
    exit 1
fi

SVC_TYPE=$(unit_get Service Type)
SVC_USER=$(unit_get Service User)
SVC_GROUP=$(unit_get Service Group)
WORKDIR=$(unit_get Service WorkingDirectory)
RESTART=$(unit_get Service Restart)
REMAIN=$(unit_get Service RemainAfterExit)
UMASK_VAL=$(unit_get Service UMask)

# systemd allows `-`, `@`, `+`, `!` prefixes on ExecStart; strip them for sh.

ONESHOT=0
if [ "$SVC_TYPE" = "oneshot" ] || [ "$REMAIN" = "yes" ]; then
    ONESHOT=1
fi

NO_RESTART=0
case "$RESTART" in
    ""|no|never) [ "$ONESHOT" = 1 ] && NO_RESTART=1 ;;
esac

# ── Generate the run script ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
RUN_SCRIPT=$(
    printf '#!/bin/sh\n'
    printf '# Generated from %s by systemd-unit-to-runit.\n' "$UNIT_FILE"
    printf '# Do not hand-edit: re-run the converter, or detach it from the unit\n'
    printf '# by deleting this header.\n'
    printf 'exec 2>&1\n\n'

    # Ordering: systemd After=/Requires= become sv waits, matching the pattern
    # used by the hand-written services in this repo.
    deps=""
    for dep in $(unit_get_all Unit After) $(unit_get_all Unit Requires); do
        case "$dep" in
            *.service)
                dep_name=${dep%.service}
                # Only wait on services that actually exist under runit.
                if [ -d "$SV_DIR/$dep_name" ]; then
                    deps="$deps $dep_name"
                fi
                ;;
        esac
    done
    if [ -n "$deps" ]; then
        cat <<'DEPFN'
wait_dep() {
    sv start "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    i=0
    until sv check "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
        i=$((i+1))
        [ "$i" -ge 90 ] && { echo "dependency $1 not ready after 90s" >&2; exit 1; }
        sleep 1
    done
}

DEPFN
        for dep_name in $deps; do
            printf 'wait_dep %s\n' "$dep_name"
        done
        printf '\n'
    fi

    # EnvironmentFile= — a leading `-` means "ignore if missing".
    env_files=$(unit_get_all Service EnvironmentFile || true)
    if [ -n "$env_files" ]; then
        printf 'set -a\n'
        printf '%s\n' "$env_files" | while IFS= read -r ef; do
            case "$ef" in
                -*) printf '[ -r %s ] && . %s\n' "${ef#-}" "${ef#-}" ;;
                *)  printf '. %s\n' "$ef" ;;
            esac
        done
        printf 'set +a\n\n'
    fi

    # Environment= — may hold several KEY=VALUE pairs per line.
    env_inline=$(unit_get_all Service Environment || true)
    if [ -n "$env_inline" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$env_inline" | while IFS= read -r line; do
            printf '%s\n' "$line" | tr ' ' '\n' | while IFS= read -r pair; do
                [ -n "$pair" ] || continue
                case "$pair" in
                    *=*) printf 'export %s\n' "$pair" ;;
                esac
            done
        done
        printf '\n'
    fi

    [ -n "$UMASK_VAL" ] && printf 'umask %s\n' "$UMASK_VAL"
    [ -n "$WORKDIR" ] && printf 'cd %s || exit 1\n' "$WORKDIR"

    # ExecStartPre= runs before the main process, same as systemd.
    pre=$(unit_get_all Service ExecStartPre || true)
    if [ -n "$pre" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$pre" | while IFS= read -r cmd; do

        done

    fi

        target="$SVC_USER"
        [ -n "$SVC_GROUP" ] && target="$SVC_USER:$SVC_GROUP"
        printf 'exec chpst -u %s %s\n' "$target" "$EXEC_START"
    else
        printf 'exec %s\n' "$EXEC_START"
    fi

    printf '# Generated from %s by systemd-unit-to-runit.\n' "$UNIT_FILE"
    printf 'exec svlogd -tt %s/%s\n' "$LOG_ROOT" "$SERVICE_NAME"

    printf '=== %s/%s/run ===\n' "$SV_DIR" "$SERVICE_NAME"
    printf '%s\n' "$RUN_SCRIPT"
    printf '\n=== %s/%s/log/run ===\n' "$SV_DIR" "$SERVICE_NAME"
    printf '%s\n' "$LOG_RUN_SCRIPT"
    exit 0

TARGET_DIR="$SV_DIR/$SERVICE_NAME"
if [ -e "$TARGET_DIR/run" ] && [ "$FORCE" != 1 ]; then
    echo "$TARGET_DIR/run already exists (use --force to overwrite)" >&2
    exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$TARGET_DIR/log"
printf '%s\n' "$RUN_SCRIPT" > "$TARGET_DIR/run"
chmod 755 "$TARGET_DIR/run"
printf '%s\n' "$LOG_RUN_SCRIPT" > "$TARGET_DIR/log/run"
chmod 755 "$TARGET_DIR/log/run"
mkdir -p "$LOG_ROOT/$SERVICE_NAME"

echo "converted $UNIT_BASE -> $TARGET_DIR/run"

    touch "$TARGET_DIR/down"
    echo "note: Restart=$RESTART — runit always restarts supervised services;" >&2
    echo "      wrote $TARGET_DIR/down so it will not auto-start." >&2
fi
if [ "$ONESHOT" = 1 ]; then
    echo "note: Type=oneshot — run it with: sv once $SERVICE_NAME" >&2
fi

# WantedBy= is systemd's enablement; the runit equivalent is a runlevel symlink.
if [ "$DO_ENABLE" = 1 ]; then
    mkdir -p "$RUNSVDIR_DEFAULT"
    ln -sfn "$TARGET_DIR" "$RUNSVDIR_DEFAULT/$SERVICE_NAME"
    echo "enabled: $RUNSVDIR_DEFAULT/$SERVICE_NAME -> $TARGET_DIR"
    echo "runsvdir scans $SERVICE_DIR automatically; no reload needed."
fi

#!/bin/sh
# op-convert-systemd-units — batch driver for the pacman hook.
#
# pacman passes the installed target paths on stdin (one per line, relative to
# the filesystem root because of `NeedsTargets`). Each .service unit is handed
# to systemd-unit-to-runit. Units that already have a runit counterpart are left
# alone so an upgrade never clobbers a hand-tuned run script.
#
# Nothing is enabled or started: a package install must not launch daemons.
set -eu

CONVERTER=${CONVERTER:-/usr/local/sbin/systemd-unit-to-runit}
SV_DIR=${SV_DIR:-/etc/runit/sv}

if [ ! -x "$CONVERTER" ]; then
    echo "op-convert-systemd-units: $CONVERTER not installed; skipping" >&2
    exit 0
fi

converted=0
skipped=0

while IFS= read -r target; do
    [ -n "$target" ] || continue
    case "$target" in
        *.service) ;;
        *) continue ;;
    esac

    # pacman emits paths without a leading slash.
    case "$target" in
        /*) unit_path=$target ;;
        *)  unit_path="/$target" ;;
    esac
    [ -f "$unit_path" ] || continue

    base=${unit_path##*/}
    svc=${base%.service}

    if [ -e "$SV_DIR/$svc/run" ]; then
        # Only replace scripts this converter generated; never a hand-written one.
        if head -3 "$SV_DIR/$svc/run" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'systemd-unit-to-runit'; then
            if "$CONVERTER" "$unit_path" --force; then
                converted=$((converted + 1))
                continue
            fi
        fi
        echo "op-convert-systemd-units: keeping existing $SV_DIR/$svc/run" >&2
        skipped=$((skipped + 1))
        continue
    fi

    if "$CONVERTER" "$unit_path"; then
        converted=$((converted + 1))
    else
        skipped=$((skipped + 1))
    fi
done

if [ "$converted" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "op-convert-systemd-units: converted $converted unit(s) to $SV_DIR"
    echo "  enable with: sudo ln -sfn $SV_DIR/<svc> /etc/runit/runsvdir/default/<svc>"
fi
[ "$skipped" -gt 0 ] && echo "op-convert-systemd-units: skipped $skipped unit(s)" >&2
exit 0

The shim is working end-to-end—the unit converted successfully, the run script executed, the enable symlink was created, and all the checks pass like is-enabled and list-unit-files. Unsupported types are being skipped and unsupported verbs are rejected as expected. Now I'm seeing a permission issue where the converter tries to create the log directory but fails because it's using the hardcoded default path instead of respecting the configured log root.

Looking at the execution order, the mkdir command is failing before the "converted" message prints, which means set -e should have aborted the converter script—but the shim continued anyway because ensure_runit_service returned via the || return 1 fallback. The service directory check still passed, so it proceeded to enable by luck. I need to make the log directory creation non-fatal by catching the error with || true and issuing a warning instead, since the converter normally runs as root via the hook but shouldn't hard-fail in other contexts.

The exit code issue turned out to be a measurement artifact from piping through head—the $? captures head's status, not the script's. Let me fix the mkdir issue and then verify the exit codes properly without any pipes.

install_control_scripts() {
    echo "Installing runit control scripts to $INSTALL_SBIN..."
    install -Dm755 "$SCRIPT_PATH" "$INSTALL_SBIN/op-runit-recompile-and-update"
    # Keep the historical s6d reload path working on runit hosts.
    install -Dm755 "$SCRIPT_PATH" "$INSTALL_SBIN/op-s6-recompile-and-update"

    # systemd compatibility layer. Third-party installers assume systemd and
    # call `systemctl enable --now X`; without these they fail and leave a
    # half-installed service. The shim goes in $INSTALL_BIN because
    # sudo's secure_path searches /usr/local/bin before /usr/bin, so it wins
    # for installers that shell out to `systemctl`.
    if [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/systemd-unit-to-runit" ]; then
        echo "Installing systemd->runit compatibility layer..."
        install -Dm755 "$SCRIPT_DIR/systemd-unit-to-runit" \
            "$INSTALL_SBIN/systemd-unit-to-runit"
        install -Dm755 "$SCRIPT_DIR/op-convert-systemd-units" \
            "$INSTALL_SBIN/op-convert-systemd-units"
        install -Dm755 "$SCRIPT_DIR/systemctl-shim" "$INSTALL_BIN/systemctl"
        # Pacman hook: convert units that packages drop, without enabling them.
        if [ -d /etc/pacman.d/hooks ] || mkdir -p /etc/pacman.d/hooks 2>/dev/null; then
            install -Dm644 "$SCRIPT_DIR/99-systemd-unit-to-runit.hook" \
                /etc/pacman.d/hooks/99-systemd-unit-to-runit.hook
        fi
    fi
}

## runit Service Management

**THIS HOST RUNS runit AS PID 1. Control services with `sv`. `systemctl` is FORBIDDEN,
and s6 is NOT installed — `s6-rc`, `s6-svc`, `s6-svstat` and `service6` do not exist.**

Runit has no compiled service database. Definitions are live files, so there is
nothing to recompile: edit the `run` script, then restart the service.

| Path | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `/etc/runit/sv/<name>/run` | The service definition |
| `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default/<name>` | Symlink that enables it at boot |
| `/run/runit/service` | The tree `runsvdir -P` supervises |
| `/etc/runit/sv/<name>/down` | Marker: do not auto-start |

### Adding a new service (exact pattern)

Service sources live in `deploy/runit/` (git-tracked), then install to
`/etc/runit/sv/`. A service is one directory with a `run` script, plus an
optional `log/run` companion:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
exec 2>&1

# Ordering: wait for dependencies to be up (runit has no dependency graph).
wait_dep() {
    sv start "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    i=0
    until sv check "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
        i=$((i+1))
        [ "$i" -ge 90 ] && { echo "dependency $1 not ready after 90s" >&2; exit 1; }
        sleep 1
    done
}
wait_dep op-session-bus

set -a
[ -r /etc/op-dbus/environment ] && . /etc/op-dbus/environment
set +a

exec chpst -u jeremy /usr/local/bin/<binary>
```

`log/run` is `#!/bin/sh` + `exec svlogd -tt /var/log/sv/<name>`.

The process **must stay in the foreground** — runit supervises the process it
starts, so a daemonising binary gets restarted in a loop. Pass the binary's
no-fork flag when it has one.

**Deploy sequence:**
```bash
sudo install -Dm755 deploy/runit/<name>/run /etc/runit/sv/<name>/run
sudo ln -sfn /etc/runit/sv/<name> /etc/runit/runsvdir/default/<name>
sudo sv start <name>          # runsvdir picks up the symlink on its own
```

To ship rebuilt binaries and restart the services using them, use the sanctioned
script rather than ad-hoc copies:
```bash
sudo deploy/runit/recompile-and-update.sh
```

**DO NOT:**
- edit `/run/runit/service/` directly — that is the supervisor's runtime view
- invoke `runsv` or `runsvdir` by hand — they belong to boot and console recovery
- expect `daemon-reload`-style steps — there is no database to reload

**Third-party installers that require systemd**: a `systemctl` shim is installed
at `/usr/local/bin/systemctl`. It maps systemd verbs onto `sv` and converts any
`.service` unit into `/etc/runit/sv/<name>/run` via
`/usr/local/sbin/systemd-unit-to-runit`. Let the installer call `systemctl`; do
not hand-translate its unit files.

input.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Keep agent sessions on the sanctioned `sv` management surface.
#
# Boot and console recovery run these programs as root and are unaffected; this
# only shadows them for interactive agent sessions.
#
# Why: runit's supervisor entry points (`runsv`, `runsvdir`, `runit-init`) are
# not service-management commands. Invoking them by hand starts a second
# supervisor or reparents services, which desynchronises /run/runit/service from
# /etc/runit/runsvdir/default and is hard to unwind. Service management goes
# through `sudo sv <command> <service>` per AGENTS.md.
#
# The s6 entry points are still listed even though the packages are not
# installed, so that reinstalling them cannot silently reopen the old path.
set -eu

GUARD_DIR=${GUARD_DIR:-/usr/local/lib/agent-runit-guard}
BIN_DIR=${BIN_DIR:-/usr/local/bin}

mkdir -p "$GUARD_DIR"

# Runit supervisor internals — not for hand invocation.
RUNIT_INTERNALS="runsv runsvdir runit runit-init utmpset"

# s6 is legacy on this host and must not come back through the side door.
S6_LEGACY="s6 s6-rc s6-rc-bundle s6-rc-compile s6-rc-db s6-rc-init \
s6-rc-update s6-svc s6-svok s6-svscan s6-svscanctl s6-svstat s6-svwait \

# Artix runit service recovery

This host boots **runit** as PID 1 and is controlled with `sv`. Runit has **no
compiled service database**, which removes the whole class of "the bootdb is
corrupt" failures that s6-rc had. There is nothing to recompile and nothing to
re-init: definitions on disk *are* the configuration.

If you arrived here looking for `s6-rc-compile`, `s6-rc-init`, or bundle
recovery: none of it applies. s6 is not installed on this host.

## Layout

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `/etc/runit/sv/<service>/run` | The service definition |
| `/etc/runit/sv/<service>/down` | Marker: do not auto-start when supervised |
| `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default/<service>` | Symlink enabling the service at boot |
| `/etc/runit/runsvdir/current` | Symlink to the active runlevel (`-> default`) |
| `/run/runit/service/<service>` | The tree `runsvdir -P` supervises |
| `/run/runit/service/<service>/supervise/` | Live state written by `runsv` |

`sv` needs root to read `supervise/ok`; an unprivileged `sv status` fails with
"access denied".

## Diagnosis order

```sh
ps -p 1 -o comm=                 # expect: runit
pgrep -a runsvdir                # expect: runsvdir -P /run/runit/service
sudo sv status <service>
ls -l /etc/runit/runsvdir/current   # which runlevel is active
```

`sv status` output reads `run: <svc>: (pid N) Ss` when healthy, `down: <svc>: Ns`
when stopped, and `warning: <svc>: unable to open supervise/ok` when `runsv` is
not supervising it at all.

## Common failures

### A service is enabled but never starts

`runsvdir` scans its directory on its own, so a missing service usually means the
symlink or the `run` script is wrong.

```sh
ls -l /etc/runit/runsvdir/default/<service>   # symlink present and not dangling?
test -x /etc/runit/sv/<service>/run           # run script executable?
sudo sh -n /etc/runit/sv/<service>/run        # syntax valid?
```

A `run` script that is not executable, or whose interpreter line is wrong, makes
`runsv` fail silently in a loop.

### A service restarts in a loop

Almost always because the process **daemonises**. Runit supervises the process it
starts; if that process forks and exits, `runsv` concludes it died and starts it
again. Fix the `run` script to keep the binary in the foreground (`-N`, `-f`,
`--foreground`, or `--nodaemon`, depending on the program) and ensure it ends
with `exec`.

### A stuck `supervise/` directory

If a service will not respond to `sv` after an unclean shutdown, the supervise
state can be stale. Stop supervision, clear the runtime view, and let `runsvdir`
re-create it:

```sh
sudo sv down <service>
sudo rm -f /run/runit/service/<service>          # runtime symlink only
# runsvdir re-creates it from /etc/runit/runsvdir/default within ~5s
sudo sv status <service>
```

Never delete `/etc/runit/sv/<service>` to fix a runtime problem — that is the
definition, not the state.

### Recovering into single-user

`/etc/runit/runsvdir/single` holds the minimal runlevel. To boot into it, append
`single` to the kernel command line, or switch at runtime:

```sh
sudo runsvchdir single      # switch runlevel
sudo runsvchdir default     # switch back
```

`runsvchdir` is the sanctioned way to change runlevels; it repoints
`/etc/runit/runsvdir/current`.

## Shipping new binaries

Do not hand-copy binaries and restart services individually. Use the sanctioned
script, which builds as the unprivileged owner of the source tree, installs to
`/usr/local/bin`, and restarts the enabled services that reference it:

```sh
sudo deploy/runit/recompile-and-update.sh
```

## Third-party installers that expect systemd

A `systemctl` shim is installed at `/usr/local/bin/systemctl`. It maps systemd
verbs onto `sv`, and converts a `.service` unit into `/etc/runit/sv/<name>/run`
using `/usr/local/sbin/systemd-unit-to-runit`. A pacman hook converts units that
packages drop, without enabling them — enabling stays an operator decision.

To convert a unit by hand and inspect the result first:

```sh
systemd-unit-to-runit /usr/lib/systemd/system/<name>.service --dry-run
sudo systemd-unit-to-runit /usr/lib/systemd/system/<name>.service --enable
```

Conversions report what runit cannot express: `Type=forking` (will restart-loop
until you add the no-fork flag), `Type=notify` (no sd_notify socket),
`Type=oneshot` (use `sv once`), and `Restart=no` (runit always restarts, so a
`down` file is written).

input.newStr:
### FR-11: A systemd compatibility wrapper converts install attempts

Third-party installers (vendor `install.sh`, pacman hooks, language package
postinstall steps) assume systemd and call `systemctl enable --now X`. On this
host those calls fail and leave a half-installed service. Three pieces close
that gap:

1. **`systemctl` shim** at `/usr/local/bin/systemctl` — maps systemd verbs onto
   `sv` (`start`, `stop`, `restart`, `reload`, `status`, `enable`, `disable`,
   `mask`, `unmask`, `is-active`, `is-enabled`, `list-units`, `cat`, `show`),
   treats `daemon-reload` as the no-op it is under runit, and refuses verbs with
   no runit meaning. `sudo`'s `secure_path` searches `/usr/local/bin` before
   `/usr/bin`, so the shim wins for installers that shell out. It prefers the
   `org.opdbus.v1.Runit.Systemctl` D-Bus service when reachable, keeping service
   changes on the audited control plane, and falls back to `sv` directly.
2. **`systemd-unit-to-runit`** at `/usr/local/sbin/` — translates one `.service`
   unit into `/etc/runit/sv/<name>/run` plus a `log/run` companion, mapping
   `ExecStart`, `ExecStartPre`, `User`/`Group` (via `chpst`), `Environment`,
   `EnvironmentFile` (honouring the optional `-` prefix), `WorkingDirectory`,
   `UMask`, and `After`/`Requires` (into `wait_dep` calls). It **reports** what
   runit cannot express rather than hiding it: `Type=forking` (would restart-loop),
   `Type=notify` (no sd_notify socket), `Type=dbus`, `Type=oneshot` (use
   `sv once`), and `Restart=no` (a `down` file is written). Template units and
   non-service unit types are refused with a clear message.
3. **Pacman hook** `99-systemd-unit-to-runit.hook` + `op-convert-systemd-units`
   — converts units that a package drops, **without enabling or starting them**:
   an install must not launch daemons, and enabling stays an operator decision.
   An existing hand-written `run` script is never overwritten; only scripts the
   converter itself generated are regenerated on upgrade.

All three install through `deploy/runit/recompile-and-update.sh`.

**Acceptance criteria**:
- `systemctl enable <unit>` on a host with only a systemd unit present generates
  `/etc/runit/sv/<name>/run` and the runlevel symlink.
- `systemctl daemon-reload` exits 0.
- `systemctl is-enabled` returns 0 when enabled, 1 when not; `is-active` returns
  3 when inactive — matching systemd's exit codes so installer logic still works.
- An unsupported verb exits 1; a `.socket`/`.timer` unit is skipped, not fatal.
- Converting a `Type=forking` unit prints the restart-loop warning.
- `systemd-unit-to-runit --dry-run` writes nothing.

Two work streams.

## Accountability audit trail (.kiro/specs/accountability-audit-trail)

durably, and replace the zeroclaw-gui Accountability stub with a real view.

  methods; the plugin's seven pre-existing methods still fall through to the

- Durability: every chain event is mirrored into the streaming blockchain's

  fails the caller. On startup the chain is replayed from disk, preserving the

  EventChainService over gRPC, decoupled from the chat path. build.rs now
  compiles op-grpc-bridge's operation.proto in place rather than copying it.

timing records, rebuilds a fresh engine from disk and re-verifies the chain.

## runit/sv migration (.kiro/specs/runit-sv-migration)

The host boots runit as PID 1 and has no s6 installed, so every s6 call site was
dead code. Removed across five layers:

- Dead spawns replaced with sv: s6-rc, s6-svc, s6-svstat, s6-svscan, s6d,
  service6 and systemctl no longer appear in any Command::new.
- op_core::runit is now the single source of truth for /etc/runit/sv,
  /etc/runit/runsvdir/default and /run/runit/service, replacing hardcoded
  /run/service, /etc/s6/sv and /run/s6-rc literals.
- Agent tools renamed s6_* -> sv_*, with sv_restart_service added because
  sv restart is native (the old map documented a stop+start workaround). Fixed
  a latent bug: the tool proxy addressed org.opdbus.s6.Systemctl, which never
  matched the daemon and always fell through to the dead s6-rc path.
- The LLM system prompt and anti-hallucination map no longer teach s6.
- Deleted crates/op-dbus: an orphaned directory with no Cargo.toml, not a
  workspace member, duplicating the migrated systemctl mapper.

  S6.Systemctl name still claimed for one release so already-installed clients
  keep working until the next recompile-and-update run.
- deploy: s6 tree removed, qdrant-grpc-loopback ported to runit, and the agent
  guard rewritten — it previously denied s6 binaries that no longer exist, so it
  guarded nothing; it now shadows the runit supervisor internals.

### systemd compatibility wrapper

Third-party installers call `systemctl enable --now X` and previously failed,
leaving half-installed services:

- deploy/runit/systemctl-shim maps systemd verbs onto sv, preferring the D-Bus
  service when reachable, and matches systemd's exit codes so installer logic
  still works.
- deploy/runit/systemd-unit-to-runit converts a .service unit into
  /etc/runit/sv/<name>/run, mapping ExecStart, ExecStartPre, User/Group via
  chpst, Environment, EnvironmentFile, WorkingDirectory, UMask and
  After/Requires. It reports what runit cannot express rather than hiding it:
  Type=forking would restart-loop, Type=notify has no sd_notify socket,
  Type=oneshot needs sv once, Restart=no gets a down file.
- A pacman hook converts units that packages drop, without enabling or starting
  them, and never overwrites a hand-written run script.

Verified: cargo check --workspace exits 0; op-state-store 41/41 tests pass;

service was restarted.

content.data:
The work is committed locally and the release build is clean. Two things need you.

**Push is blocked — no credentials on this host.** The commit `352c0ad3` (66 files, +6908/−1743) sits on `agent/zeroclaw-runtime-routing` ready to go, but `origin` is HTTPS and there's no credential helper, no `~/.git-credentials`, no SSH key, and `gh` isn't logged in. Any of these unblocks it: `gh auth login`, adding an SSH key and switching the remote to `git@github.com:`, or a PAT. I staged only real content changes — this repo reports ~2500 files as modified from filemode noise, so I unstaged 52 mode-only entries to keep the commit reviewable.

**Release build: 33 binaries, 0 errors, 12m 32s.** Including `op-grpc-bridge` (104M), `op-s6-systemctl`, `s6d`, `op-cognitive-mcp`, `zeroclaw-gui`, and `opdbus`. Note it needs `CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint"` because vendored RocksDB in `cozorocks 0.1.7` won't compile on this GCC — worth fixing separately, since the deploy script's `sudo -u` build would hit it.

**btrfs send can't proceed yet.** The layout from `deploy/btrfs-layout.sh` doesn't exist on this host: no `/opt/op-dbus`, no `modules`/`snapshots`/`staging` mounts, and `btrfs subvolume list /` shows no `@op-dbus-*` subvolumes. So there's nothing to snapshot and no configured receive side. I need from you: the send target (host or container), and whether to run `deploy/btrfs-layout.sh` first to create the subvolumes — that one formats layout on a live filesystem, so I'd want your go-ahead rather than assuming.

On your correction: I had written in three places that `recompile-and-update.sh` was the way to ship binaries. That was wrong, and I've fixed AGENTS.md, `docs/operations/artix-runit-recovery.md`, and the LLM system prompt to say deployment is btrfs send/receive of subvolume snapshots, with the script demoted to local dev iteration only. That's now in the amended commit.

What landed in the migration, beyond the s6→runit port you asked me to bring over: every dead `Command::new("s6-*"/"service6"/"s6d")` replaced with `sv`; `op_core::runit` as the single source of truth for the three runit paths; agent tools renamed `s6_*`→`sv_*` with `sv_restart_service` added since `sv restart` is native; the LLM prompt and anti-hallucination map no longer teach s6; the orphaned `crates/op-dbus/` deleted; and the systemd compatibility wrapper you asked for — a `systemctl` shim plus a unit converter, tested against all 11 real systemd units on this host, which reports what runit can't express (`Type=forking` would restart-loop) instead of silently emitting a broken service. A `cargo test` guard now fails if any of it regresses; it caught seven sites I'd missed, including `Command::new("systemctl")` in `op-state/authority.rs`.

input.__tool_use_purpose: Script that builds the golden deployment subvolume and installs to the live runtime in parallel

input.content:
#!/bin/sh
# build-golden.sh — publish a release two ways, from one build.
#
#   1. GOLDEN  — populate the `golden` btrfs subvolume and take a read-only
#                snapshot. The snapshot is the artifact `btrfs send` ships;
#                nothing else is a deployment source.
#   2. LIVE    — install the same binaries into this host's runtime
#                (/usr/local/bin, /etc/runit/sv) and restart only the runit
#                services whose binary actually changed.
#
# Both read the same `target/release`, so the golden snapshot and the running
# host are provably the same build — the MANIFEST records per-binary sha256 so
# that can be checked after the fact.
#
# Layout created under $OPDBUS_ROOT (default /opt/op-dbus):
#
#   golden/                      read-write staging subvolume
#     bin/                       release binaries
#     sbin/                      control scripts + systemd compat layer
#     sv/<service>/run           runit service definitions
#     etc/                       environment defaults, pacman hooks
#     MANIFEST                   commit, build time, sha256 per binary
#   snapshots/deploy/golden-<UTC>/   read-only snapshot (the send source)
#
# Usage:
#   build-golden.sh                 # both paths (default)
#   build-golden.sh --golden-only   # skip touching the running host
#   build-golden.sh --live-only     # skip the subvolume/snapshot
#   build-golden.sh --no-restart    # install live but leave services running old code
#   build-golden.sh --send user@host:/path/to/receive
#   build-golden.sh --dry-run
#
# Requires root for the subvolume and the live install. Never builds: run
# `CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build --workspace --release` first (the
# vendored RocksDB in cozorocks needs that flag on modern GCC).
set -eu

OPDBUS_ROOT=${OPDBUS_ROOT:-/opt/op-dbus}
GOLDEN_DIR="$OPDBUS_ROOT/golden"
SNAPSHOT_DIR="$OPDBUS_ROOT/snapshots/deploy"

INSTALL_BIN=${INSTALL_BIN:-/usr/local/bin}
INSTALL_SBIN=${INSTALL_SBIN:-/usr/local/sbin}
RUNIT_SV_DIR=${RUNIT_SV_DIR:-/etc/runit/sv}
RUNIT_RUNSVDIR=${RUNIT_RUNSVDIR:-/etc/runit/runsvdir/default}

DO_GOLDEN=1
DO_LIVE=1
DO_RESTART=1
DRY_RUN=0
SEND_TARGET=""

SCRIPT_PATH=$(readlink -f "$0" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$0")
SCRIPT_DIR=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$SCRIPT_PATH")" && pwd)
if [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../Cargo.toml" ]; then
    PROJECT_ROOT=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
else
    PROJECT_ROOT=${OP_DBUS_ROOT:-$(pwd)}
fi
RELEASE_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/target/release"

log()  { printf '\033[0;34m[golden]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[0;32m[ ok  ]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[warn ]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { printf '\033[0;31m[fail ]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

run() {
    if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
        printf '  would run: %s\n' "$*"
    else
        "$@"
    fi
}

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --golden-only) DO_LIVE=0 ;;
        --live-only)   DO_GOLDEN=0 ;;
        --no-restart)  DO_RESTART=0 ;;
        --dry-run)     DRY_RUN=1 ;;
        --send)        shift; [ $# -gt 0 ] || die "--send needs a target"; SEND_TARGET=$1 ;;
        -h|--help)     sed -n '2,40p' "$SCRIPT_PATH"; exit 0 ;;
        *)             die "unknown option: $1" ;;
    esac
    shift
done

# ── Preconditions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[ -d "$RELEASE_DIR" ] || die "no $RELEASE_DIR — build first:
  CXXFLAGS=\"-include cstdint\" cargo build --workspace --release"

BINARIES=$(find "$RELEASE_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -executable ! -name '*.d' ! -name '*.so' | sort)
[ -n "$BINARIES" ] || die "$RELEASE_DIR contains no executables"
BIN_COUNT=$(printf '%s\n' "$BINARIES" | wc -l)
log "$BIN_COUNT release binaries in $RELEASE_DIR"

if [ "$DRY_RUN" != 1 ] && [ "$(id -u)" != 0 ]; then
    die "must run as root (subvolume creation and install to $INSTALL_BIN)"
fi

COMMIT=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
STAMP=$(date -u '+%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ')

# ═══ Path 1: golden subvolume ═══════════════════════════════════════════════
build_golden() {
    log "building golden subvolume at $GOLDEN_DIR"

    # /opt must be btrfs for subvolumes; refuse rather than silently making a
    # plain directory that cannot be snapshotted or sent.
    fstype=$(stat -f -c %T "$OPDBUS_ROOT" 2>/dev/null || stat -f -c %T "$(dirname "$OPDBUS_ROOT")")
    case "$fstype" in
        btrfs) ;;
        *) die "$OPDBUS_ROOT is on '$fstype', not btrfs — snapshots and send need btrfs" ;;
    esac

    run mkdir -p "$OPDBUS_ROOT" "$SNAPSHOT_DIR"

    if [ ! -d "$GOLDEN_DIR" ]; then
        run btrfs subvolume create "$GOLDEN_DIR"
        ok "created subvolume $GOLDEN_DIR"
    else
        log "reusing existing subvolume $GOLDEN_DIR"
    fi

    run mkdir -p "$GOLDEN_DIR/bin" "$GOLDEN_DIR/sbin" "$GOLDEN_DIR/sv" "$GOLDEN_DIR/etc"

    # Binaries
    printf '%s\n' "$BINARIES" | while IFS= read -r bin; do
        run install -Dm755 "$bin" "$GOLDEN_DIR/bin/$(basename "$bin")"
    done
    ok "staged $BIN_COUNT binaries into golden/bin"

    # Control scripts + the systemd compatibility layer.
    for script in systemd-unit-to-runit op-convert-systemd-units systemctl-shim \
                  recompile-and-update.sh; do
        [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/$script" ] &&
            run install -Dm755 "$SCRIPT_DIR/$script" "$GOLDEN_DIR/sbin/$script"
    done
    [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/../agent-runit-guard.sh" ] &&
        run install -Dm755 "$SCRIPT_DIR/../agent-runit-guard.sh" \
            "$GOLDEN_DIR/sbin/agent-runit-guard.sh"
    ok "staged control scripts into golden/sbin"

    # Runit service definitions tracked in the repo.
    for svc_dir in "$SCRIPT_DIR"/*/; do
        [ -f "${svc_dir}run" ] || continue
        svc=$(basename "$svc_dir")
        run mkdir -p "$GOLDEN_DIR/sv/$svc"
        run install -Dm755 "${svc_dir}run" "$GOLDEN_DIR/sv/$svc/run"
        [ -f "${svc_dir}log/run" ] &&
            run install -Dm755 "${svc_dir}log/run" "$GOLDEN_DIR/sv/$svc/log/run"
        [ -f "${svc_dir}finish" ] &&
            run install -Dm755 "${svc_dir}finish" "$GOLDEN_DIR/sv/$svc/finish"
    done
    ok "staged runit service definitions into golden/sv"

    # Config the target needs alongside the binaries.
    [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/../environment.default" ] &&
        run install -Dm644 "$SCRIPT_DIR/../environment.default" \
            "$GOLDEN_DIR/etc/environment.default"
    [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/99-systemd-unit-to-runit.hook" ] &&
        run install -Dm644 "$SCRIPT_DIR/99-systemd-unit-to-runit.hook" \
            "$GOLDEN_DIR/etc/pacman-hooks/99-systemd-unit-to-runit.hook"
    [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/../99-agent-runit-guard.hook" ] &&
        run install -Dm644 "$SCRIPT_DIR/../99-agent-runit-guard.hook" \
            "$GOLDEN_DIR/etc/pacman-hooks/99-agent-runit-guard.hook"

    # MANIFEST: what this snapshot is, and the hashes to prove the running host
    # matches it.
    if [ "$DRY_RUN" != 1 ]; then
        {
            printf 'golden-build: %s\n' "$STAMP"
            printf 'commit: %s\n' "$COMMIT"
            printf 'source: %s\n' "$PROJECT_ROOT"
            printf 'init: runit (sv)\n'
            printf 'binaries: %s\n' "$BIN_COUNT"
            printf '\n[sha256]\n'
            printf '%s\n' "$BINARIES" | while IFS= read -r bin; do
                printf '%s  %s\n' "$(sha256sum "$bin" | cut -d' ' -f1)" "$(basename "$bin")"
            done
        } > "$GOLDEN_DIR/MANIFEST"
    fi
    ok "wrote golden/MANIFEST (commit $COMMIT)"

    # Read-only snapshot — this, not `golden/`, is what gets sent.
    SNAPSHOT_PATH="$SNAPSHOT_DIR/golden-$STAMP"
    run btrfs subvolume snapshot -r "$GOLDEN_DIR" "$SNAPSHOT_PATH"
    ok "snapshot ready to send: $SNAPSHOT_PATH"

    if [ -n "$SEND_TARGET" ]; then
        log "btrfs send -> $SEND_TARGET"
        case "$SEND_TARGET" in
            *:*)
                host=${SEND_TARGET%%:*}
                path=${SEND_TARGET#*:}
                if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
                    printf '  would run: btrfs send %s | ssh %s btrfs receive %s\n' \
                        "$SNAPSHOT_PATH" "$host" "$path"
                else
                    btrfs send "$SNAPSHOT_PATH" | ssh "$host" "btrfs receive $path"
                    ok "sent to $SEND_TARGET"
                fi
                ;;
            *)
                run sh -c "btrfs send '$SNAPSHOT_PATH' > '$SEND_TARGET'"
                ok "wrote send stream to $SEND_TARGET"
                ;;
        esac
    fi
}

# ═══ Path 2: live runtime ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Which enabled services reference a given binary in their run script?
services_using() {
    binary=$1
    for link in "$RUNIT_RUNSVDIR"/*; do
        [ -e "$link" ] || continue
        svc=$(basename "$link")
        run_script="$RUNIT_SV_DIR/$svc/run"
        [ -f "$run_script" ] || continue
        if grep -q "$binary" "$run_script" 2>/dev/null; then
            printf '%s\n' "$svc"
        fi
    done
}

install_live() {
    log "installing into the live runtime"

    changed_binaries=""
    printf '%s\n' "$BINARIES" | while IFS= read -r bin; do
        name=$(basename "$bin")
        target="$INSTALL_BIN/$name"
        if [ -f "$target" ] && cmp -s "$bin" "$target"; then
            continue
        fi

#!/bin/sh
# build-golden.sh — publish a release two ways, from one build.
#
#   1. GOLDEN  — populate the `golden` btrfs subvolume and take a read-only
#                snapshot. The snapshot is the artifact `btrfs send` ships;
#                nothing else is a deployment source.
#   2. LIVE    — install the same binaries into this host's runtime
#                (/usr/local/bin, /etc/runit/sv) and restart only the runit
#                services whose binary actually changed.
#
# Both read the same `target/release`, so the golden snapshot and the running
# host are provably the same build — the MANIFEST records per-binary sha256 so
# that can be checked after the fact.
#
# Layout created under $OPDBUS_ROOT (default /opt/op-dbus):
#
#   golden/                      read-write staging subvolume
#     bin/                       release binaries
#     sbin/                      control scripts + systemd compat layer
#     sv/<service>/run           runit service definitions
#     etc/                       environment defaults, pacman hooks
#     MANIFEST                   commit, build time, sha256 per binary
#   snapshots/deploy/golden-<UTC>/   read-only snapshot (the send source)
#
# Usage:
#   build-golden.sh                 # both paths (default)
#   build-golden.sh --golden-only   # skip touching the running host
#   build-golden.sh --live-only     # skip the subvolume/snapshot
#   build-golden.sh --no-restart    # install live but leave services running old code
#   build-golden.sh --send user@host:/path/to/receive
#   build-golden.sh --dry-run
#
# Requires root for the subvolume and the live install. Never builds: run
# `CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build --workspace --release` first (the
# vendored RocksDB in cozorocks needs that flag on modern GCC).
set -eu

OPDBUS_ROOT=${OPDBUS_ROOT:-/opt/op-dbus}
GOLDEN_DIR="$OPDBUS_ROOT/golden"
SNAPSHOT_DIR="$OPDBUS_ROOT/snapshots/deploy"

INSTALL_BIN=${INSTALL_BIN:-/usr/local/bin}
INSTALL_SBIN=${INSTALL_SBIN:-/usr/local/sbin}
RUNIT_SV_DIR=${RUNIT_SV_DIR:-/etc/runit/sv}
RUNIT_RUNSVDIR=${RUNIT_RUNSVDIR:-/etc/runit/runsvdir/default}

DO_GOLDEN=1
DO_LIVE=1
DO_RESTART=1
DRY_RUN=0
SEND_TARGET=""

SCRIPT_PATH=$(readlink -f "$0" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$0")
SCRIPT_DIR=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$SCRIPT_PATH")" && pwd)
if [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../Cargo.toml" ]; then
    PROJECT_ROOT=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
else
    PROJECT_ROOT=${OP_DBUS_ROOT:-$(pwd)}
fi
RELEASE_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/target/release"

log()  { printf '\033[0;34m[golden]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[0;32m[ ok  ]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[warn ]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { printf '\033[0;31m[fail ]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

run() {
    if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
        printf '  would run: %s\n' "$*"
    else
        "$@"
    fi
}

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --golden-only) DO_LIVE=0 ;;
        --live-only)   DO_GOLDEN=0 ;;
        --no-restart)  DO_RESTART=0 ;;
        --dry-run)     DRY_RUN=1 ;;
        --send)        shift; [ $# -gt 0 ] || die "--send needs a target"; SEND_TARGET=$1 ;;
        -h|--help)     sed -n '2,40p' "$SCRIPT_PATH"; exit 0 ;;
        *)             die "unknown option: $1" ;;
    esac
    shift
done

# ── Preconditions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[ -d "$RELEASE_DIR" ] || die "no $RELEASE_DIR — build first:
  CXXFLAGS=\"-include cstdint\" cargo build --workspace --release"

BINARIES=$(find "$RELEASE_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -executable ! -name '*.d' ! -name '*.so' | sort)
[ -n "$BINARIES" ] || die "$RELEASE_DIR contains no executables"
BIN_COUNT=$(printf '%s\n' "$BINARIES" | wc -l)

    die "must run as root (subvolume creation and install to $INSTALL_BIN)"
fi

COMMIT=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
STAMP=$(date -u '+%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ')

# ═══ Path 1: golden subvolume ═══════════════════════════════════════════════
build_golden() {
    log "building golden subvolume at $GOLDEN_DIR"

    # /opt must be btrfs for subvolumes; refuse rather than silently making a
    # plain directory that cannot be snapshotted or sent.
    fstype=$(stat -f -c %T "$OPDBUS_ROOT" 2>/dev/null || stat -f -c %T "$(dirname "$OPDBUS_ROOT")")
    case "$fstype" in
        btrfs) ;;
        *) die "$OPDBUS_ROOT is on '$fstype', not btrfs — snapshots and send need btrfs" ;;
    esac

    run mkdir -p "$OPDBUS_ROOT" "$SNAPSHOT_DIR"

    if [ ! -d "$GOLDEN_DIR" ]; then
        run btrfs subvolume create "$GOLDEN_DIR"
        ok "created subvolume $GOLDEN_DIR"
    else
        log "reusing existing subvolume $GOLDEN_DIR"
    fi

    run mkdir -p "$GOLDEN_DIR/bin" "$GOLDEN_DIR/sbin" "$GOLDEN_DIR/sv" "$GOLDEN_DIR/etc"

    # Binaries
    printf '%s\n' "$BINARIES" | while IFS= read -r bin; do
        run install -Dm755 "$bin" "$GOLDEN_DIR/bin/$(basename "$bin")"
    done
    ok "staged $BIN_COUNT binaries into golden/bin"

    # Control scripts + the systemd compatibility layer.
    for script in systemd-unit-to-runit op-convert-systemd-units systemctl-shim \
                  recompile-and-update.sh; do
        [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/$script" ] &&
            run install -Dm755 "$SCRIPT_DIR/$script" "$GOLDEN_DIR/sbin/$script"
    done
    [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/../agent-runit-guard.sh" ] &&
        run install -Dm755 "$SCRIPT_DIR/../agent-runit-guard.sh" \
            "$GOLDEN_DIR/sbin/agent-runit-guard.sh"
    ok "staged control scripts into golden/sbin"

    # Runit service definitions tracked in the repo.
    for svc_dir in "$SCRIPT_DIR"/*/; do
        [ -f "${svc_dir}run" ] || continue
        svc=$(basename "$svc_dir")
        run mkdir -p "$GOLDEN_DIR/sv/$svc"
        run install -Dm755 "${svc_dir}run" "$GOLDEN_DIR/sv/$svc/run"
        [ -f "${svc_dir}log/run" ] &&
            run install -Dm755 "${svc_dir}log/run" "$GOLDEN_DIR/sv/$svc/log/run"
        [ -f "${svc_dir}finish" ] &&
            run install -Dm755 "${svc_dir}finish" "$GOLDEN_DIR/sv/$svc/finish"
    done
    ok "staged runit service definitions into golden/sv"

    # Config the target needs alongside the binaries.
    [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/../environment.default" ] &&
        run install -Dm644 "$SCRIPT_DIR/../environment.default" \
            "$GOLDEN_DIR/etc/environment.default"
    [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/99-systemd-unit-to-runit.hook" ] &&
        run install -Dm644 "$SCRIPT_DIR/99-systemd-unit-to-runit.hook" \
            "$GOLDEN_DIR/etc/pacman-hooks/99-systemd-unit-to-runit.hook"
    [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/../99-agent-runit-guard.hook" ] &&
        run install -Dm644 "$SCRIPT_DIR/../99-agent-runit-guard.hook" \
            "$GOLDEN_DIR/etc/pacman-hooks/99-agent-runit-guard.hook"

    # MANIFEST: what this snapshot is, and the hashes to prove the running host
    # matches it.
    if [ "$DRY_RUN" != 1 ]; then
        {
            printf 'golden-build: %s\n' "$STAMP"
            printf 'commit: %s\n' "$COMMIT"
            printf 'source: %s\n' "$PROJECT_ROOT"
            printf 'init: runit (sv)\n'
            printf 'binaries: %s\n' "$BIN_COUNT"
            printf '\n[sha256]\n'
            printf '%s\n' "$BINARIES" | while IFS= read -r bin; do
                printf '%s  %s\n' "$(sha256sum "$bin" | cut -d' ' -f1)" "$(basename "$bin")"
            done
        } > "$GOLDEN_DIR/MANIFEST"
    fi
    ok "wrote golden/MANIFEST (commit $COMMIT)"

    # Read-only snapshot — this, not `golden/`, is what gets sent.
    SNAPSHOT_PATH="$SNAPSHOT_DIR/golden-$STAMP"
    run btrfs subvolume snapshot -r "$GOLDEN_DIR" "$SNAPSHOT_PATH"
    ok "snapshot ready to send: $SNAPSHOT_PATH"

    if [ -n "$SEND_TARGET" ]; then
        log "btrfs send -> $SEND_TARGET"
        case "$SEND_TARGET" in
            *:*)
                host=${SEND_TARGET%%:*}
                path=${SEND_TARGET#*:}
                if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
                    printf '  would run: btrfs send %s | ssh %s btrfs receive %s\n' \
                        "$SNAPSHOT_PATH" "$host" "$path"
                else
                    btrfs send "$SNAPSHOT_PATH" | ssh "$host" "btrfs receive $path"
                    ok "sent to $SEND_TARGET"
                fi
                ;;
            *)
                run sh -c "btrfs send '$SNAPSHOT_PATH' > '$SEND_TARGET'"
                ok "wrote send stream to $SEND_TARGET"
                ;;
        esac
    fi
}

# ═══ Path 2: live runtime ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Which enabled services reference a given binary in their run script?
services_using() {
    binary=$1
    for link in "$RUNIT_RUNSVDIR"/*; do
        [ -e "$link" ] || continue
        svc=$(basename "$link")
        run_script="$RUNIT_SV_DIR/$svc/run"
        [ -f "$run_script" ] || continue
        if grep -q "$binary" "$run_script" 2>/dev/null; then
            printf '%s\n' "$svc"
        fi
    done

    changed_binaries=""
    printf '%s\n' "$BINARIES" | while IFS= read -r bin; do
        name=$(basename "$bin")
        target="$INSTALL_BIN/$name"
        if [ -f "$target" ] && cmp -s "$bin" "$target"; then
