        fi
        run install -Dm755 "$bin" "$target"
        printf '%s\n' "$name" >> /tmp/golden-changed.$$
    done
    [ -f "/tmp/golden-changed.$$" ] && changed_binaries=$(cat "/tmp/golden-changed.$$")
    rm -f "/tmp/golden-changed.$$"

    fi

    # secure_path searches it before /usr/bin, so it wins for installers.
    for script in systemd-unit-to-runit op-convert-systemd-units; do
        [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/$script" ] &&
            run install -Dm755 "$SCRIPT_DIR/$script" "$INSTALL_SBIN/$script"
    done
    [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/systemctl-shim" ] &&
        run install -Dm755 "$SCRIPT_DIR/systemctl-shim" "$INSTALL_BIN/systemctl"
    [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/../agent-runit-guard.sh" ] &&
        run install -Dm755 "$SCRIPT_DIR/../agent-runit-guard.sh" \
            "$INSTALL_SBIN/agent-runit-guard"
    ok "installed control scripts + systemd compat layer"

    if [ -d /etc/pacman.d/hooks ] || mkdir -p /etc/pacman.d/hooks 2>/dev/null; then
        [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/99-systemd-unit-to-runit.hook" ] &&
            run install -Dm644 "$SCRIPT_DIR/99-systemd-unit-to-runit.hook" \
                /etc/pacman.d/hooks/99-systemd-unit-to-runit.hook

    # script that differs (the host copy is authoritative until an operator says
    # otherwise).
    for svc_dir in "$SCRIPT_DIR"/*/; do
        [ -f "${svc_dir}run" ] || continue
        svc=$(basename "$svc_dir")
        dest="$RUNIT_SV_DIR/$svc/run"

            continue
        fi
        run install -Dm755 "${svc_dir}run" "$dest"
        [ -f "${svc_dir}log/run" ] &&

    done

#!/bin/sh
# build-golden.sh — publish a release two ways, from one build.
#
#   1. GOLDEN  — populate the `golden` btrfs subvolume: the deployable content.
#                Taking the read-only snapshot and running `btrfs send` belongs
#                to the deployment process, not here. This script only makes
#                `golden` correct and current.
#   2. LIVE    — install the same binaries into this host's runtime
#                (/usr/local/bin, /etc/runit/sv) and restart only the runit
#                services whose binary actually changed.
#
# Both read the same `target/release`, so the golden subvolume and the running
# host are provably the same build — the MANIFEST records per-binary sha256 so
# that can be checked after the fact.
#
# Layout created under $OPDBUS_ROOT (default /opt/op-dbus):
#
#   golden/                      the deployable subvolume
#     bin/                       release binaries
#     sbin/                      control scripts + systemd compat layer
#     sv/<service>/run           runit service definitions
#     etc/                       environment defaults, pacman hooks
#     MANIFEST                   commit, build time, sha256 per binary
#
# Usage:
#   build-golden.sh                 # both paths (default)
#   build-golden.sh --golden-only   # skip touching the running host
#   build-golden.sh --live-only     # skip the subvolume
#   build-golden.sh --no-restart    # install live but leave services running old code
#   build-golden.sh --dry-run
#
# Requires root for the subvolume and the live install. Never builds: run
# `CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build --workspace --release` first (the
# vendored RocksDB in cozorocks needs that flag on modern GCC).
set -eu

OPDBUS_ROOT=${OPDBUS_ROOT:-/opt/op-dbus}
GOLDEN_DIR="$OPDBUS_ROOT/golden"

INSTALL_BIN=${INSTALL_BIN:-/usr/local/bin}
INSTALL_SBIN=${INSTALL_SBIN:-/usr/local/sbin}
RUNIT_SV_DIR=${RUNIT_SV_DIR:-/etc/runit/sv}
RUNIT_RUNSVDIR=${RUNIT_RUNSVDIR:-/etc/runit/runsvdir/default}

DO_GOLDEN=1
DO_LIVE=1
DO_RESTART=1
DRY_RUN=0

    if [ -n "$SEND_TARGET" ]; then
        log "btrfs send -> $SEND_TARGET"
        case "$SEND_TARGET" in
            *:*)
                host=${SEND_TARGET%%:*}
                path=${SEND_TARGET#*:}
                if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
                    printf '  would run: btrfs send %s | ssh %s btrfs receive %s\n' \

                else
                    btrfs send "$SNAPSHOT_PATH" | ssh "$host" "btrfs receive $path"
                    ok "sent to $SEND_TARGET"
                fi
                ;;
            *)
                run sh -c "btrfs send '$SNAPSHOT_PATH' > '$SEND_TARGET'"
                ok "wrote send stream to $SEND_TARGET"
                ;;
        esac
    fi

The restart list is pulling in too many services — 13 total, including critical networking components like OVS, DHCP, and session bus services. Since this is a remote machine, restarting those network-related services could sever the connection entirely, which is a significant risk I need to avoid.

The root cause is overly broad substring matching in the grep logic. When searching for a binary like "opdbus", it's matching "opdbus-rundirs" and other unrelated services. The matching also triggers on any mention of the binary in run scripts, even in comments, which is too loose. I need to anchor the match to the actual installed path with proper word boundaries — matching only when the exact binary path is being executed, not just mentioned anywhere in the script.

But there's a bigger safety concern: restarting network services on a remote host is risky. Even with correct matching, services like `ovsbr0-uplink` legitimately reference their own binaries, and auto-restarting them could sever connectivity. I should implement an explicit exclusion list for network-critical services that require manual operator intervention rather than automatic restarts.

I'll add a NEVER_AUTO_RESTART list, do a dry-run to show the user what would be restarted, and get confirmation before executing anything.

Implementing the fixes now...

content.data: Two problems in that restart list. The matching is substring-based (`opdbus` matches `opdbus-rundirs`), and it would restart `ovs-vswitchd`, `ovsbr0-uplink`, and `uplink-dhcp` — on a remote host that risks cutting network access. Fixing both:

input.__tool_use_purpose: Fix substring matching and protect network-critical services from auto-restart
input.command: strReplace
input.newStr:
# Services that are never auto-restarted: they carry the host's network and
# session bus, and bouncing them from a deploy script can cut remote access or
# reparent the control plane. They are reported so an operator can restart them
# deliberately, on the console, in a chosen order.
NEVER_AUTO_RESTART="ovs-vswitchd ovsbr0-addr ovsbr0-svc-addr ovsbr0-uplink \
uplink-dhcp op-session-bus opdbus-rundirs dbus"

# Which enabled services actually exec a given binary?
#
# Matches the installed path with a trailing word boundary, not the bare name:
# a substring match would tie `opdbus` to `opdbus-rundirs` and drag unrelated
# services into the restart set.
services_using() {
    binary=$1
    # `.` is the only ERE metacharacter in these paths.
    escaped=$(printf '%s' "$INSTALL_BIN/$binary" | sed 's/\./\\./g')
    for link in "$RUNIT_RUNSVDIR"/*; do
        [ -e "$link" ] || continue
        svc=$(basename "$link")
        run_script="$RUNIT_SV_DIR/$svc/run"
        [ -f "$run_script" ] || continue
        if grep -qE "${escaped}([^A-Za-z0-9_.-]|\$)" "$run_script" 2>/dev/null; then
            printf '%s\n' "$svc"
        fi
    done
}

The dry run is now correct and safe. Here's exactly what a real run would do:

**Golden subvolume** (`/opt/op-dbus/golden`, created as a btrfs subvolume): 33 binaries in `bin/`, control scripts plus the systemd compat layer in `sbin/`, 3 runit service definitions in `sv/`, config and pacman hooks in `etc/`, and a `MANIFEST` recording commit `352c0ad3` with per-binary sha256. No snapshot, no send — that's deploy-time, per your correction.

**Live runtime**: same 33 binaries into `/usr/local/bin`, the `systemctl` shim, converter and guard, then restart **4** services: `op-cognitive-mcp`, `op-grpc-bridge`, `op-of-controller`, `op-web`.

Two safety findings from the dry run, both worth your attention:

`ovs-vswitchd` is held back rather than restarted. It matched because `op-ovsbr0-setup` changed, but bouncing it on a remote host risks the uplink. Same protection covers `ovsbr0-*`, `uplink-dhcp`, `op-session-bus`, `opdbus-rundirs`, and `dbus` — reported for deliberate console action instead.

My first draft would have restarted **13** services including `ovsbr0-uplink` and `uplink-dhcp`, which could have cut network access. Two bugs caused that: the service matcher grepped for bare binary names, so `opdbus` matched `opdbus-rundirs`; and I'd defined the exclusion list without applying it. Both fixed — matching is now against the full install path with a word boundary, and the filter actually runs.

Also surfaced: `/etc/runit/sv/notebook-sources-sync/run` and `xray-config-mount/run` differ from the repo copies. The script leaves the host versions alone rather than clobbering hand-tuning — you may want to reconcile those separately.

On the recompile script: you were right, it was a legacy artifact — it installed itself as `op-s6-recompile-and-update` for the "historical s6d reload path." Deleted, and `build-golden.sh` replaces it. AGENTS.md, the recovery doc, and the LLM system prompt now point at `build-golden.sh`.

I have **not** run it for real. It creates a subvolume under `/opt` and restarts four control-plane services including the gRPC bridge. Say go and I'll execute, then verify each with `sv status`. If you'd rather stage it, `--golden-only` builds the deployable subvolume without touching the running host.
